name: level-bubble
title: Level Bubble
description: A spirit level for a value against its target: a 16px-tall capsule holds two tolerance ticks and a floating ring that shows signed deviation on an underdamped spring, resting calm inside the ticks and pressing against the capsule end when out of band — the printed deviation ('+3.2%') is always beside it.
useWhen: anything monitored against a two-sided target rather than a one-sided maximum — SLO error-budget burn pace, burn rate vs plan, temperature vs setpoint, throughput vs quota — where the question is 'how far off am I, and which way', answered by a bubble that can sit on either side of dead-center; pick feeler-gap instead for a one-sided go/no-go check (value vs a limit it must stay under) or ration-rule for a static used/total allowance with no notion of overshoot in either direction. Also distinct from reed-vu, which reads unsigned live loudness with no target at all.
instruction: Renders one live reading — `value` against a `target`, both in the same units — as a spirit level rather than a gauge or badge. A 16px-tall, full-radius capsule (inline SVG rect, rx = half its height) is outlined in --border only, no fill; two hairline vertical ticks sit inside it at ± `tolerance` on-scale from dead center, stroked in `var(--warning, #f5a623)` — the one and only place that token appears, matching the repo rule that warning marks a threshold, never recolors a value. A 10px ring (--foreground stroke, `fill=none` — an air bubble, not a solid dot) floats along the capsule's horizontal axis; its resting x position is `deviation = value - target` normalized against an optional `range` prop (defaults to 3x tolerance, so the ticks sit comfortably inside the track rather than at its very edge) and clamped to ±1, so a value equal to target centers the bubble exactly on the capsule's midline and the ticks are the only other thing that ever gets an on-scale position. The bubble never animates via CSS transition or React state per frame — its x is written straight to the circle ref's `transform: translateX()` on a hand-rolled requestAnimationFrame loop integrating an underdamped spring (stiffness 180, damping 14, mass 1, semi-implicit Euler, dt capped at 32ms) toward that normalized target every time `value` or `target` changes, so live data makes it swing past its resting point with a lazy overshoot before settling rather than snapping or gliding predictably — the loop sleeps once position and velocity both drop under a small epsilon and wakes again on the next prop change. Outside the tolerance ticks the bubble's clamp keeps it from ever leaving the capsule shape — it can only press up to the inner wall at full deflection, which reads as pressure rather than an escape. Whether a reading counts as 'outside tolerance' is computed directly from `value`/`target`/`tolerance` every render, never from the animated position, so a spring's transient overshoot through the tick line during a big swing never flickers the visual state on its own — only a genuinely out-of-band prop value does. That boolean drives two things in the same beat: the capsule's own outline `stroke-width` doubles (1.5px -> 3px, CSS-transitioned), and the deviation readout printed in Geist Mono directly beside the capsule — signed, one decimal, e.g. '+3.2%' or '-1.1°F', always visible regardless of state so the bubble is never the sole channel for the reading — steps from font-weight 400 to 600. Structurally the gauge is `role=meter` with `aria-labelledby` pointing at the visible uppercase label, `aria-valuemin` = target - range, `aria-valuemax` = target + range, `aria-valuenow` = value, and `aria-valuetext` phrased as the deviation itself rather than the raw value — e.g. '3.2 percent over target, outside tolerance' or '1.1 degrees under target, within tolerance' or 'on target, within tolerance' at dead center — built from an optional `unitLabel` prop (falls back to the short `unit` used in the printed row) exactly like the repo's other meters split their short glyph from their spoken word. A separate visually-hidden `role=status`/`aria-live=polite` paragraph announces only on an outside-tolerance transition (entering or leaving the band), not on every value tick, so a fast-moving live feed doesn't spam assistive tech the way a continuously-updating live region would; the meter's own `aria-valuetext` still updates every render for anyone who focuses it directly. The SVG is `aria-hidden` and, being a display-only meter with no exposed control, is correctly exempt from the registry's tab-reachability check, matching feeler-gap and ration-rule. Under `prefers-reduced-motion` (checked via `matchMedia` with a change listener) the spring loop is skipped entirely — the bubble's x snaps straight to its resting position via a CSS `transform 100ms linear` transition instead, still visibly eased rather than a hard cut, per the reduced-motion spec of a 100ms linear ease. Every stroke is `stroke-current` colored by a `text-border`/`text-foreground`/`text-muted` class except the two tolerance ticks, so both themes restyle for free. Differs from reed-vu, which visualizes unsigned live loudness off a real AnalyserNode with no target and no notion of direction, and from tide-gauge-password, which fills a reservoir toward a single maximum — level-bubble is the only one of the three answering a signed, two-sided question: how far off, and which way.
